Dear Dr. Jenkins,

Thank you for evaluating Mr. Mark Collins, a 46-year-old accountant whom I am referring to your care for an urgent nephrological consultation. 

Mr. Collins recently re-established care with our practice. Routine laboratory evaluation revealed profound, advanced native renal failure, with his serum creatinine measuring 5.8 mg/dL and his estimated GFR now down to 11 mL/min/1.73m². The exact chronicity and onset of his renal decline are unknown, as he has not had routine medical evaluations or blood testing for quite some time. 

On physical examination today, he is comfortable and in no acute distress. Blood pressure is 126/78 mmHg, pulse is 70 beats per minute, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Cardiac auscultation reveals regular rate and rhythm with no murmurs, rubs, or gallops. Lungs are clear bilaterally. His abdomen is soft, non-tender, and without hepatosplenomegaly. Examination of the extremities demonstrates no peripheral edema. His joints display full range of motion without erythema or warmth, and there is no history or clinical evidence of gout. 

His only medication is amlodipine 5 mg daily. He does not use tobacco, consumes alcohol only socially, and his family history is non-contributory. 

Given the severity of his renal functional decline, I would be grateful for your formal assessment and guidance regarding definitive management and planning for long-term renal replacement therapy.

Sincerely,

Dr. Arthur Davies
